dogecoin.text:
I grew up listening to adults regretting how instead of buying a Royal Enfield if they bought the shares of Eicher Motors back in the day, they would be so much wealthier.

I don't like regrets so I put my hard-earned money in the very reliable Dogecoin instead of buying a dog.
So if Dogecoin is so easily manipulated by one influential individual, is it not fundamentally against the core principle of decentralisation?
